items.title: ATP: The Energy Currency of Cells

source_refs.note: ATP: The Energy Currency of Cells, printed pages 141-142 (PDF 144-145); a main subheading of Bioenergetics and ATP: the energy currency of cells, its own page as in Computer Science (owner 2026-11-04).

blocks.text: Cells use a special energy currency for their reactions. This currency is actually a nucleotide called adenosine triphosphate (ATP). When cells store energy, they make ATP. When cells need energy, they break ATP. A molecule of ATP has three subunits i.e. adenine, (a nitrogen containing base); ribose (a five-carbon sugar) and three phosphate groups.

blocks.alt: Three phosphate groups, drawn as circles marked P, in a row joined by wavy lines labelled Energy bonds; the third phosphate is joined to a pentagon labelled Ribose, which is joined to a fused five- and six-membered double ring labelled Adenine. Nested coloured bands with double arrows mark Adenosine (adenine and ribose), Adenosine monophosphate (AMP), Adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and Adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
blocks.caption: Figure 5.1: Molecular structure of ATP (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.1).

blocks.text: ATP was discovered in 1929 by Karl Lohmann. In 1941, the Nobel prize winner, Fritz Lipmann proposed that ATP is the main energy-transfer molecule in the cell.

The covalent bonds between two phosphates are high-energy bonds. When one of these bonds is broken, inorganic phosphate (Pi) separates and energy is released. The breaking of one phosphate bond releases about 7.3 kcal (7,300 calories) per mole of ATP.

blocks.text_alt: ATP + H₂O → ADP + Pᵢ + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)

blocks.text: In common energy reactions only the outer P-P high-energy bond breaks. When this happens, ATP becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and one Pi is released.
In some cases, ADP is further broken down to AMP (adenosine monophosphate) and Pi:

blocks.text_alt: ADP + H₂O → AMP + Pᵢ + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)

blocks.text: Cells get energy from the oxidation of food. They store this energy by combining ADP with Pi to form ATP. So, we can summarize that ATP is made during energy-releasing processes and it is broken down during energy-consuming processes. In this way ATP transfers energy between metabolic reactions.

blocks.alt: A cycle between a blue ball ATP on the left and a green ball ADP on the right. The upper arrow, Formation of ATP, runs from ADP to ATP, with Energy and Pi going in. The lower arrow, Breakdown of ATP, runs from ATP to ADP, with Water going in and Pi and Energy coming out.
